_comment: Same-game correlation rules for 2-leg parlays (Rule 3). Legs from different games are always 'neutral'. For two legs of the same game the rules are tried top to bottom, in both leg orders, and the first match decides. Labels: positive (allowed under same_game_policy positive_only), negative (rejected under positive_only), neutral (rejected under positive_only, allowed under any), exclusive (both legs cannot win: always rejected), redundant (double-counts one outcome: always rejected).

_leg_fields.kind: side (spread or moneyline) | total | team_total | prop
_leg_fields.cls: market class: side, total, team_total, or the cls of a prop market in markets.json (pass_yds, pass_tds, completions, interceptions, rush_yds, rush_att, rec_yds, receptions, rush_rec_yds, anytime_td, first_td); 'any_prop' matches every prop
_leg_fields.dir: up = Over / Yes (more offence, or the team winning for sides), down = Under / No
_leg_fields.family: stat families from markets.json; two legs on the same player sharing a family double-count

_relations: same_player, other_player, same_team, other_team, same_market, same_family, same_direction, opposite_direction; favored_by_at_least: N (the side leg's team is favoured by at least N points, moneylines converted to a point equivalent)

rules.label: exclusive
rules.reason: the same player cannot go over and under the same stat

rules.label: redundant
rules.reason: two lines on one player's same stat family (rush yards and rush + rec yards, receptions and receiving yards, anytime and first TD) double-count one outcome

rules.label: exclusive
rules.reason: only one player scores the first touchdown

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: one player's volume and scoring move together (passing yards and passing TDs, receiving yards and anytime TD)

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: one player's stats rarely split high and low in the same game

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a quarterback's passing yards are his receivers' receiving yards; both over (or both under) move together

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a quarterback over with his receiver under (or the reverse) pulls in opposite directions

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a receiver's touchdown is a passing touchdown

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: two receivers on one team compete for the same targets; both going over is unlikely

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a quiet passing game keeps every receiver under

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a pass-heavy script and a run-heavy script compete for the same plays

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: teams that lead run the ball; a rushing over goes with the team winning or covering

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a rushing over against the opponent winning or covering; in a blowout the trailing team stops running

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a rushing under with the team winning pulls in opposite directions

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a team that trails abandons the run

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: passing volume rises when trailing and falls when leading, so a passing over and the team winning do not reinforce each other

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: interceptions lose games

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: the opponent benefits from interceptions

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a team that scores touchdowns tends to win

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a touchdown for one team and the other team winning pull apart

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a player's production and his team's points move together (anytime TD + team total over, team total over + passing TDs over)

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a player's production over with his team's points under contradicts itself

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: passing and scoring production rise with the game total

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: production over with the game total under contradicts itself

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: rushing volume and the game total are only loosely linked

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: a player's production and the opponent's points are only loosely linked

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: players on opposite teams share a game but not a resource; book pricing may still treat them as correlated

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: no specific rule links these two teammates' stats

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: no specific rule links this stat to the game result

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: spread and moneyline on the same team win together (a duplicate line is simply positive)

rules.label: exclusive
rules.reason: both sides of one spread or moneyline cannot win

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: one team's spread against the other's moneyline pulls apart

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: two overs (or two unders) on the game total

rules.label: exclusive
rules.reason: over and under of the game total cannot both win

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: two overs (or two unders) on one team's total

rules.label: exclusive
rules.reason: over and under of one team's total cannot both win

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: the two teams' totals are only loosely linked

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a team that scores more tends to win or cover (Home ML + Home team total Over)

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a team winning while scoring little pulls apart

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: the opponent scoring more makes winning harder (Home ML + Away team total Over trap)

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: holding the opponent down goes with winning

rules.label: positive
rules.reason: a team's points are part of the game total

rules.label: negative
rules.reason: a team over with the game under (or the reverse) pulls apart

rules.label: neutral
rules.reason: the game total says nothing about which team wins
